# Vendored sibling crates (pinned mirrors)

These directories are byte-for-byte copies (`git archive <sha>:crates/<name>`)
of sibling crates at the revisions the pipeline was built against when each
was last re-pinned. **These are frozen snapshots, not live mirrors**: as of
this writing every pinned SHA checked except `compiler` (`math-layout`
`ea4ee5c8`, `font-resources`/`project-files` `d5440b0`, `font-engine`
`f418238`, `pdf` `bffd168a`, `document-style` `bfc980d`,
`paragraph-layout`/`tex-text-encoding`/`tex-boxes`/`tex-expansion` `87a513de`,
`microtype` `8193d5db`) is an ancestor of `main` — i.e. `main` has since moved
on, by anywhere from nothing at all
(`tex-text-encoding`/`tex-boxes`/`tex-expansion`, which have had no commits since
their pin) through 8 (`math-layout`) to over 2500 (`document-style`,
`font-engine`) —
so these pins are **behind `main`**, not ahead of it, except where a
directory's own row says its source branch is still unmerged: `vector-graphics`
is pinned from `agent/kabir-claude/tikz-min` (though that pin's content is
currently byte-identical to `main`'s `crates/vector-graphics`), and `compiler`
is pinned from `engine/letter-class-compiler` (PR #316), which is `main` plus
one commit — that row says when to move it back. Re-verify with
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <pin-sha> HEAD` before trusting either direction,
since both sides move. They exist only so `crates/render-pipeline` builds
standalone from a `git archive` of this directory alone (which is how the
visual-oracle harness builds it). They are
read-only here: no edits, no fixes; requested API changes go to the owning
agent through `docs/proposals/rendering-abi.md` and are listed in the
render-pipeline README. Each directory carries a `PIN` file with the full
commit SHA it was exported from. Directory names are the plain crate names
because the siblings depend on each other by `../<name>` path.

| Directory | Branch | Commit | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Byte-identity verified two independent ways, as this row's older re-pins were: `git ls-tree -r faa7d484 crates/compiler` matches a mode+blob-SHA listing of the vendored tree on all **562** files, and `diff -r --exclude=PIN` against a fresh `git archive faa7d484 crates/compiler` extraction is empty. Three moved compiler APIs had no pipeline handling and are the whole of this re-pin's pipeline diff; none was swallowed by a wildcard arm. (1) `Inline::HFill` gained `leader: FillLeader` (#320, `\hrulefill`/`\dotfill`). The **glue** is now set — both are `\leavevmode\leaders<box>\hfill\kern\z@`, so the pipeline emits the existing `Item::LeaveVmode`, the `\hfill`, and a zero `Item::Kern`; all three are load-bearing. The `\leavevmode` keeps a lone `\hrulefill` paragraph from being dropped with the `\vspace` in front of it (that took `enumitem-worksheet` from 3 pages to 2), and the `\kern\z@` stops TeX's end-of-paragraph final-glue deletion (tex.web §816, `hlist`'s trailing-glue loop) from eating a trailing fill. The **leader box is not painted**: the pipeline has no leaders outside `typeset/toc.rs`'s `leader_dots`, and `flashtex-paragraph-layout` reports no per-glue set width (only `Line::ratio`/`set_width`/`items` and box positions), so painting them is its own change. Each occurrence is therefore lowered with a new typed `unsupported_inline` warning naming `\hrulefill` or `\dotfill` — never dropped silently. Measured on `fixtures/divergence-probes/min-hrulefill`, whose README recorded `Date:` landing 198.51 bp left of pdflatex: it is now **0.55 bp** from the oracle's x 317.830 (the residual is the unpainted leader). (2) `Diagnostic` gained `labels`, `notes` and `help` (#346/#389) on top of the `code`/`suggestion` already forwarded (#354). display-list-v2's `diagnostic` object is `additionalProperties: false` over exactly `{code, message, severity, sources}` (`protocol/rendering-v2.schema.json`), so inventing wire fields is the protocol owner's call, not a re-pin's; `Diagnostic::from_compiler` folds them onto the fields that already mean the same thing instead — label spans join `sources` (deduplicated against the diagnostic's own span, `maxItems` 128 respected), and label texts, notes and the help message become bracketed `[note: …]`/`[help: …]` clauses on `message` (`maxLength` 4096), with `help.replacement` back-filling runtime-v1's `suggestion` when the legacy field is unset. They stay on **one line**: `flashtex-render --tex` prints `severity[code] message (line:col)` per line, and an embedded newline strands the position suffix (caught by `tests/cli_e2e.rs`). Appending a clause also has to stay invisible to everything that matches on the compiler's *phrasing*: `packages::supersede_message` drops or trims the `packages … are recognised but not implemented` diagnostic for the packages this crate sets on the compiler's behalf (`implemented_by_pipeline`: amsmath, amssymb, amsfonts, lmodern, microtype, geometry, graphicx, tikz), and it ends its match with `strip_suffix`, so the first version of this folding made **every one of those leak** into the render output — each telling the reader the pipeline had not set something it had. `supersede_message` and `preamble_command_superseded` now run on the body: a new `split_clauses` peels trailing clauses off before matching and re-attaches them to whatever survives a trimmed list. It keys on the clause *shape* (` [<label>: <text>]`, bracket-depth aware) rather than the two labels that exist today, so a third kind appended later needs no further fix. (3) `Inline::Underline` (#328/#390, ulem `\uline`/`\sout` and kernel text `\underline`) is implemented for real by **PR #329**, which was written for exactly this re-pin ("needs vendor/compiler re-pin"), is pipeline-only, and applied cleanly here; its `UnderlineItem`/`Item::Underline` geometry is already measured against pdflatex to 0.01 pt. Its one integration gap was a `pagebuild::VBlock` literal predating `broken_penalty`, set to `Vec::new()` because the underlined fragment is one unbreakable line. `tests/uline.rs` 2/2 and `tests/underline_sout.rs` 4/4. One behaviour change does come from the pin itself: this compiler emits `unsupported_feature` "packages amsmath are recognised but not implemented" for `\usepackage{amsmath}` where `e44d5917` did not (`package_matches_layout` keeps amsmath out on purpose — *the compiler's own* v1 layout does not implement it). That line never reaches a consumer, because `packages::supersede_message` drops it; it was visible during this re-pin only because the clause folding above had broken that supersede, which is the bug described there rather than a second one. `font-engine` enables its `paragraph`/`math`/`pdf` adapter features by
default, which is why those three siblings must be present under their plain
names next to it.

`font-resources` brings `serde`, `serde_json` and `sha2` from the registry
(the first external crates in this build); everything else is path-only.

**Delete this directory and point `Cargo.toml` path dependencies at
`../<name>` once render-pipeline's own build no longer needs a standalone
`git archive` of pinned sources** — as of this writing `main` is already
*ahead* of every pin here (see the note above), so the blocker is not that
`main` lacks these changes; it's that `render-pipeline` still depends on
frozen copies instead of the live `../<name>` siblings. Nothing binary is vendored; Latin Modern's OTFs
and TFMs are read from the local TeX Live installation at run time, never
committed; the 12 pt TFM set is digest-bound to the official Latin Modern
2.004 release (`REQUIRED_TFMS` in `src/fonts.rs`).
